images.filename: Beaumaris men of the 23rd of Foot who fell in WWI - geograph.org.uk - 914313.jpg
images.caption:
Beaumaris men of the 23rd of Foot who fell in WWI The 23rd of Foot was formed in the year of the Battle of the Boyne. The Regiment, one of only four in the British Army to retain its independence until 2006, won 14 Victoria Crosses. The history of the Royal Welch as a fighting unit extends back to the Battle of Aughrim in 1691. Since then it has fought in the eighteenth century campaigns of Marlborough, the American War of Independence, the wars with Revolutionary and Napoleonic France, the Crimean War, the Boer War. the First and Second World War and the Gulf War, as well as serving as peace keepers in Northern Ireland and Bosnia.
On 1st March 2006 the three Welsh infantry regiments combined to form a new regiment  The Royal Welsh. The new title of the Royal Welch Fusiliers is:
1st Battalion The Royal Welsh (The Royal Welch Fusiliers).

images.filename: Atlas Van der Hagen-KW1049B11 052-Twee scenes- -1- VLUGT VAN JACOB DE II uyt Ierland naar Vrankrijk, den 12 Iuly 1690 -2- OVERWINNING VAN KON. WILLEM DE III. door het volkomen slaan van Jacob de II. in Ierland den 11 Iuly 1690.jpeg
images.caption: In 1689, stadholder William III had forced Jacob II Stuart from the English throne. Jacob II fled to safety to Louis XIV of France, while William III took his place on the English throne. Jacob tried to recover his throne in England in 1690 using a military expedition via Ireland. This was frustrated by William III who succeeded in conquering a combined French/Irish army in the Battle at the river Boyne on 11 July 1690. This print by Romeyn de Hooghe (1645-1708) shows two scenes important for the Republic. Top of the print: the flight of Jacob II to France. Bottom, a scene from the glorious campaign of William III.
